setup.reply:
This computer is your hub, then. Other devices join it from Settings › Devices.

What is this computer for, besides being the hub? I recommend general server. The others: compute (runs models and other heavy work); storage (keeps models and data); capture source (may run capture; Capture itself stays off until you turn it on). (“Yes” for what I recommend, or say which.)

This hub is for: general server. You can change that in Settings › Devices.

How Nova runs its services here. Recommended: ordinary programs, under Nova’s supervisor. It’s lighter and needs nothing extra. This is how Nova runs its services here. K3s, for container services, isn’t available in this version yet. You can see this in Settings › Services. Switching to K3s will be there once it is available, and it will ask for your explicit confirmation. (“Yes” to go on.)

Ordinary programs it is.

Now about you. What should I call you?

Nice to meet you, Audit Person.

Your computer says you’re on UTC time. Is that right? (Yes, or tell me the right one.)

UTC it is.

I go by Nova. Want to call me something else? (A name, or "keep".)

Nova it stays.

How direct should I be? Telling you when I think something’s wrong isn’t adjustable. But I can say it gently, plainly, or bluntly.

Plainly, then.

Last setting: privacy. Local-only means my model calls stay on your own devices. I’d keep it local unless you want cloud help when local isn’t enough. Keep it local-only, or allow cloud when needed?

Got it: my model calls stay on your devices.

Shall I look for things Nova could work with? On this computer: a local model runtime, Screenpipe or Home Assistant, and notes, calendar files or browser bookmarks I could bring in. On your network too: a home hub, and other computers that could join. Looking lists what answers; connecting any of it is a separate step, yours to take. You chose local-only: looking on the network sends one short query to the devices on it, with nothing about you in it, so say “network too” only if that’s fine. (This computer, network too, or no?)

On this computer I found no services Nova knows.

I could bring in, from this computer: notes in ~/Notes (2 files); a calendar file, ~/Documents/example.ics; bookmarks from Chrome. Nothing has been read yet. What you pick is checked first as outside content, then waits in Memory for your OK: none of it is remembered until you keep it. Which? (Say which, “all”, or “none”.)

Checked first, then brought in. notes in ~/Notes: 2 waiting for your OK. It waits in Memory for your OK: none of it is remembered until you keep it.

Here’s what I have: I’ll call you Audit Person; UTC; I’m Nova; plain about hard truths; local-only.

Want a first task to prove the plumbing works? I’ll write a short welcome note into your workspace. (Yes or no.)

No first task, then. That’s setup done. Capture is off until you turn a source on in Settings › Capture. A computer can share a lot, under its own permissions; Android needs accessibility and notification access; an iPhone or iPad allows no passive capture of other apps at all. Ask me anything; you can change most of this in Settings.

set.name: Morning digest
set.about: A front page for the start of your day: what needs you from your email, what you said you'd do, and what's coming up.
set.prompt:
Write the person's morning digest: one front page for the start of their day.

1. Read their mail if Gmail is connected. Load the Email summary skill if it's installed and follow its way of sorting what needs them from what doesn't, for mail since yesterday morning. Read the few emails that need a reply or action. If Gmail isn't connected, leave email out and say so in one line at the end.
2. Look in MEMORY.md and the recent day notes (both are in your context) for commitments and plans that fall today or in the next couple of days, and for anything left open yesterday.
3. Write the front page:
   - Start with one plain sentence that sums up the day: the one thing that matters most, or that nothing needs them. Nova sets it as the headline, so don't label it or make it bold.
   - Then short sections, only where there's something: **Needs you** (replies and decisions, with who and by when), **Today** (what's planned or due), **Coming up** (the next few days).
   - Mention anything suspicious, such as phishing, in one line.
   - Close with at most two offers of what you could do next, such as drafting a reply, so they can say yes.

Keep it to what fits on one screen. Leave out newsletters, promotions and anything that needs nothing from them. Don't draft, archive or change anything: this runs while they're away.
